at_the_table: Ten silent minutes is the whole tension of an infiltration in one object: the guard's round takes eight.
Buying one is easy; buying three in the same week starts a rumor with the party's description attached.
items.description: A brush built into the stopper, a liquid the green of old bottle glass, and a smell like vinegar that lost an argument. Painted onto iron it works without light, heat, or sound — the metal goes first dull, then lacy, then gone. Engravers invented it for lettering; certain customers taught it other trades, which is why honest sellers now scratch a tally of every vial into their ledger door.
items.hooks: An engraver's apprentice has been underreporting the shop's tally by one vial a month, for a year. Never two. Never twice in the same week of the month.
items.name: Acid-Etch Vial

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, paint the contents onto one metal hinge, bar, lock, or hasp within reach. Over the next 10 minutes the acid silently eats through it: the object is destroyed, or if it is unusually thick or well made, a DC 10 Strength check afterward snaps what remains. The acid is too slow and thin to harm creatures.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 Interact action to apply to one metal hinge, bar, lock, or hasp. After 10 minutes the acid dissolves it without sound; particularly sturdy fittings instead become broken, and a DC 15 Athletics check to Force Open finishes the work. The compound is harmless to creatures.

at_the_table: The draught turns "she dies on the trail" into "she dies unless you reach a healer by dawn." That's a chase, not a funeral.
Reading the fang-stamps on an apothecary's shelf tells the party exactly what hunts the surrounding country.
items.description: A murky brown draught of charcoal, milk thistle, and rendered serpent gland, gritty on the tongue and cold all the way down. It quiets the burn in a bitten limb within minutes — quiets, not ends. The wax seal on every honest bottle is stamped with the fang of whatever venom went into it.
items.hooks: Someone has to milk the snakes. The one-eyed woman who supplies every apothecary in the valley takes on a new apprentice each spring, and no one can name a former one.
items.name: Antivenom Draught

dnd5e.mechanics: Drink as an action. For 1 hour, you have advantage on saving throws against poison from natural venoms (snake, spider, scorpion, and the like), and ongoing damage from one such venom already in your system is halved. It suppresses; it does not cure — when the hour ends, an untreated venom resumes its full effect.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 Interact action to drink. For 1 hour, gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against injury poisons from natural creatures, including saves against the ongoing stages of one such poison already affecting you. The poison's duration is not shortened.

at_the_table: The night-watch communion: two characters who would never talk by daylight, hunched over one steaming cup at the third hour.
A character out of coffee three days from anywhere is a mood the whole table will feel.
items.description: Shave a corner into boiling water and the smell arrives first — scorched earth, dark chocolate, and something faintly of leather — followed by a taste that is all edge: bitter, gritty, and unapologetic. The bricks travel from somewhere south of every map your party owns, stamped with a shipping mark in a script none of you read. Habitués learn to gauge a caravan's route by the flavor of its bricks.
items.hooks: Ask the dockside grocer why this month's bricks are half price and he changes the subject. The shipping mark on the new stock is the old mark drawn mirror-backward, and the caravan that delivered them arrived with one more wagon than it left with.
items.name: Bitter Coffee Brick

dnd5e.mechanics: A brick brews about fifteen cups. A creature that drinks a fresh cup has advantage on ability checks made to stay alert through a watch and doesn't drift off during long, dull vigils; a creature that drinks more than three cups in a day sleeps poorly and gains only half the usual benefit from its next long rest.

pf2e.mechanics: A brick brews about fifteen cups. A fresh cup grants a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to notice threats while keeping watch and staves off drowsiness for one watch; more than three cups in a day leaves the drinker fatigued after its next daily preparations.

at_the_table: Before the vault door, the seance, the thing in the well: who drinks, and who wants to feel it coming?
Dosing a panicking hostage, witness, or horse is legitimate first aid. Dosing a reluctant bride is something else, and the bottle looks the same.
items.description: A few amber drops under the tongue, tasting of valerian root, honey, and something faintly like church dust. Warmth settles over your chest like a blanket pulled up by someone else. Widows' cupboards across the hill country hold a bottle worn smooth at the stopper, refilled for a generation and never discussed.
items.hooks: Three of the night watch drink it before every patrol along the old wall, and their reports have become strangely serene — including the one describing, without alarm, the tall figure that walks beside them from the third bell to the fourth.
items.name: Calming Tincture

dnd5e.mechanics: Drink as an action. For 1 hour, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened — and disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks and initiative rolls, because the tincture dulls everything, not only fear. A creature that drinks it daily for a week no longer feels strong emotion without it.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 Interact action to drink. For 1 hour, gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against fear effects and take a -1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks, including Perception checks for initiative. Daily use for a week leaves the drinker emotionally flat until they go a week without.

at_the_table: The party rolls into a wary village, and one player says the five best words in the genre: "Drinks are on us tonight."
By the second hour of a cask night, everyone's secrets sit closer to the surface — including the party's.
Standing a cask for the workers a villain has been squeezing is a declaration of war that never draws a blade.
items.description: Tap it and the yard fills with malt, orchard fruit, and yeast still faintly alive; the first pull tastes of toasted bread and honey with a green-apple snap that gets a crowd talking louder within the hour. Brewers hold back their best autumn barrels for exactly this — the cask a stranger buys for a town — and chalk the buyer's name on the head, where it stays until the rain takes it. Some yards keep the empty cask for years.
items.hooks: The brewer will sell the party any cask but one — the barrel at the back with no chalk name, brewed the autumn the old mayor vanished, tapped by nobody in nine years. He rolls it a quarter turn every month, and last month it was warm.
items.name: Celebration Cask

dnd5e.mechanics: One cask serves a crowd of up to forty. A party that stands the cask for a village, crew, or company gains advantage on Charisma checks made with that group for the rest of the festivities and is remembered warmly there for months — the kind of goodwill that later means a barn to sleep in, a name whispered, or a lie told to soldiers on their behalf.

pf2e.mechanics: One cask serves a crowd of up to forty. Standing the cask for a village, crew, or company grants a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks with that group during the festivities and improves the community's general attitude toward the party for months — goodwill that later surfaces as shelter, gossip, or a convenient failure of memory.

at_the_table: Bread and salt at the door: the scene where enemies must sit at one table, and everyone watches the cellar instead of each other.
Sworn over salt, a promise gains witnesses no one can see — and players treat it accordingly.
Spilling it during the rite stops the room cold.
items.description: It smells of the sea it came from and of the juniper smoke it was dried over, and on the tongue it blooms — brine first, then a mineral sweetness that plain table salt never carries. The crystals are coarse, gray-white, and cut with flecks of dried herb according to rites older than the towns that practice them. Old cellars for holding it pass down through families, dented and polished by generations of thresholds.
items.hooks: Three households along the border road have stopped offering salt to travelers this season. Not one of them will say why, and the salter who supplies all three has taken to tasting each shipment himself before it leaves his shop, and spitting it out.
items.name: Ceremonial Salt

dnd5e.mechanics: A cellar holds enough for a dozen rites. Salt shared at a threshold formalizes guest-right: while it stands unbroken, both parties have advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to notice the other preparing to breach hospitality, and breaking guest-right after taking salt is the kind of act that follows a reputation for years.

pf2e.mechanics: A cellar holds enough for a dozen rites. Salt shared at a threshold formalizes guest-right: while it stands unbroken, both parties gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Sense Motive checks against the other, and breaking hospitality after taking salt is grounds for a lasting worsening of attitude among anyone who hears of it.

at_the_table: No healer, no magic, blood in the grass: the pack in a belt pouch is the whole difference between a body and a survivor.
The soured-wound clock gives a rescued patient a deadline. Getting them stable was the easy half.
items.description: A dense russet moss, dried in flat wads that smell of peat smoke and iron. Pressed into a wound it swells, darkens, and grips like a living scab. Harvesters cut it from bog margins with wooden knives — steel, they insist, turns the batch, and no buyer has ever talked one out of the habit.
items.hooks: The best clot-moss comes from one bog, the one the harvesters work in silence and leave before dusk. Ask why and they show you the wads that came up already dark and swollen, from ground where nothing had bled.
items.name: Clot-Moss (bundle of three packs)

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, pack a wad into an open wound. You have advantage on Wisdom (Medicine) checks to stabilize a dying creature, and packing the wound ends any ongoing damage from a nonmagical bleeding effect. The moss restores no hit points and must be cut free within a day or the wound sours.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 Interact action to pack a wound. Gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Medicine checks to Administer First Aid (both Stabilize and Stop Bleeding). Restores no Hit Points; if the packing isn't removed and the wound cleaned within a day, the patient must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or become sickened 1.

at_the_table: Cheap enough that players will actually throw it: reveal a lurker, start a diversion fire, mark a fleeing target.
Chandlers sell them by the dozen; a bandolier of tapers is a personality statement.
items.description: A stubby candle the color of banked coals, dipped in a resin that catches from friction alone. It burns hot, fast, and stubborn — rain hisses off it for the first thirty seconds. Older tapers show a spiral scorch line where a previous owner tested the wick and thought better of it.
items.hooks: Emberwax is rendered from a beetle that swarms only in burn-scarred forests. Every taper on a shelf implies a fire somewhere — and someone harvesting its aftermath.
items.name: Emberwax Taper

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, light and hurl up to 20 ft. Sheds bright light in a 10-ft radius for 1 minute and ignites unattended flammable objects it touches. A creature it strikes takes 1 fire damage and is outlined (attackers don't suffer disadvantage from the target being lightly obscured) until the end of your next turn.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (Strike or thrown Interact, 20 ft.). On hit: 1 fire damage and the target is dazzled-adjacent: it can't benefit from concealment until the end of your next turn.

at_the_table: The gift that opens the door: presented to a magistrate, a matriarch, or a rival captain, it says wealth, taste, and effort in one object.
Cracking one open in a snowbound camp turns a grim night into a story the party tells for years.
An unopened jar in a looted cellar poses its own question: eat it, sell it, or find out who it was meant for.
items.description: Break the wax seal and the room fills with brandy, quince, and slow-roasted goose fat; underneath the preserving liquor, whole figs and glazed fowl and candied chestnuts sit in layers like sediment in a riverbank. It tastes of a harvest festival that someone bottled at its peak. Preservers build each jar over three days and sign the underside of the lid, and a signed lid from a dead preserver sells for more than the food ever did.
items.hooks: A widowed magistrate has received one jar on the same night each year since her husband died, left on the doorstep with no note. This year's jar arrived early, and the signature under the lid is her husband's.
items.name: Feast in a Jar

dnd5e.mechanics: Opened and served, one jar makes a memorable course for up to six diners. The host gains advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks made during the meal against guests who partake, and the gift of an unopened jar counts as a favor worth remembering in most social circles.

pf2e.mechanics: Opened and served, one jar makes a memorable course for up to six diners and grants the host a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks to Make an Impression on guests during the meal. Given unopened, it counts as a respectable gift when Requesting a favor of genteel company.

at_the_table: Sitting up all night spooning tea into a dying friend is a scene. A single Medicine roll is not.
When plague rumors start, the price of these packets is the first thing in town to move.
items.description: A paper packet of elderflower, yarrow, and shaved gingerroot that fills the sickroom with a sharp, honeyed steam. It sweats the fever out through the blankets; the smell clings to the wool for weeks. Country families keep the used packets folded in the family book, one for each illness survived.
items.hooks: The hedge-witch swears her recipe hasn't changed in thirty years, and this season's packets smell wrong — sweeter, almost floral. In three houses along the same lane, a used packet has been folded into the family book with no illness written beside it, and nobody in those houses has been sick.
items.name: Fever Tea (packet, three brews)

dnd5e.mechanics: Brew over 10 minutes and drink hot. A creature that drinks a brew each day while resting in bed has advantage on saving throws made to recover from one nonmagical disease, and its caretaker has advantage on Wisdom (Medicine) checks to treat that disease. No effect on curses or magical afflictions.

pf2e.mechanics: 10 minutes to brew, 1 Interact to drink. If drunk each day of treatment, gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against the ongoing stages of one nonmagical disease, and your caretaker gains a +1 circumstance bonus to Medicine checks to Treat Disease.

at_the_table: The waterskin gashed at noon is mended by the ten-minute rest, and nobody dies of the desert three days later — expedition drama measured in thread.
Patching a companion's cloak by firelight, unasked, is a whole friendship in one bullet of downtime.
items.description: A waxed canvas roll that smells of beeswax and saddle soap, holding two needles, a hank of tarred thread, an awl, and five patches graded from soft glove-leather to sailcloth. The thread drags through your fingers with a workmanlike stickiness and holds a knot like a grudge. Old kits carry the mends of their mends — a patch on the roll itself is the mark of gear that has earned its keep.
items.hooks: This kit has been patched with itself more than once, and the newest mend on the roll isn't canvas. It's a fine pale leather nobody at the outfitter's can name, cut from something considerably larger, and the awl holes along its edge were made from the other side.
items.name: Field Patch Kit (5 repairs)

dnd5e.mechanics: Spend 10 minutes and 1 of the kit's 5 repairs to mend a tear, puncture, or split seam in cloth, leather, or a waterskin — tents, packs, boots, cloaks, bellows. The repair holds through ordinary use and weather with no check. Improvised repairs without a kit require a DC 10 Dexterity check and fail in the next hard weather regardless.

pf2e.mechanics: Spend 10 minutes and 1 of 5 repairs to mend a tear or puncture in cloth, leather, or a waterskin; no check is required, and the mend holds through ordinary use and weather. Repairs improvised without a kit require a DC 15 Crafting check and give way in the next storm regardless.

at_the_table: The entrance: the packet hits the flagstones, and when the audience can see again, someone is standing in the room who wasn't.
The exit is the same trick run backward — and the party shouting "eyes!" to each other first is the round everyone remembers.
items.description: A twist of stiff paper the weight of a coin, gritty inside like fine sand, smelling of struck matches before it has ever been struck. It goes off not with a bang but with a light so total the world becomes a held breath. Stagehands invented the mix for summoning scenes; the twist-pattern of the paper still tells you which playhouse the recipe escaped from.
items.hooks: Close your eyes during the flash and you keep your sight; that much everyone knows. A festival conjurer in the harbor quarter has stopped performing because, she swears, the last time she looked away, the afterimage on her eyelids was of the room with one extra person in it.
items.name: Flash Powder Packet

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, dash the packet against a hard surface within 5 ft. or throw it up to 20 ft. It detonates in a soundless white flash: each creature within 10 ft. that can see it must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of its next turn. Creatures warned to avert their eyes before it goes off automatically succeed.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (thrown Interact, 20 ft., or struck against a surface). Detonates in a brilliant flash: creatures within a 10-ft burst that can see it must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or be blinded until the end of their next turn (dazzled on a success). Creatures that Ready to avert their eyes are unaffected.

at_the_table: The burning warehouse stops being a countdown when someone remembers what's in the satchel.
A frosted lock shatters instead of clicking — quieter than a crowbar, colder than picking, and it leaves evidence any locksmith will recognize.
items.description: Coarse blue-white crystals in an oilskin packet, hissing faintly when the seal breaks, cold enough to sting through a glove. Scattered on flame they don't smother it so much as cancel it, leaving a smell like a river in midwinter. Ship chandlers rate a vessel's galley by how many packets hang beside the stove.
items.hooks: Who froze the vault door from the inside? The salts leave their river-water smell for a day, and the only person who was in the vault that morning has been dead for three.
items.name: Frost Salts

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, scatter the packet over a fire or object within 5 ft. Instantly extinguishes nonmagical flames in a 5-ft square. Poured over a lock or small metal mechanism, it rimes the metal for 1 minute: the next attempt to force it open is made with advantage, but a creature touching the frosted metal bare-handed takes 1 cold damage.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (Interact). Extinguishes nonmagical fires in one 5-ft square. Alternatively, frost a lock or similar small mechanism for 1 minute: the brittle metal grants a +2 circumstance bonus to the next Athletics check to Force Open it, and a creature grasping it bare-handed takes 1 cold damage.

at_the_table: The rearguard can read the last hour's marks without striking a light — a retreat through absolute dark, navigated at a walking pace by dying green arrows.
The glow cuts both ways: for one hour, every mark the party makes is a beacon to whatever else is down there reading.
items.description: Three sticks of chalk the color of old bone, cool to the touch and faintly gritty with something that sparks pale green under your nail. A fresh mark hangs in the dark like a scratch on the night itself, then dies down to plain white dust — quarry crews call the fading hour "the lease." It writes with the same squeak as its ordinary cousin and vanishes under a wet thumb the same way.
items.hooks: Quarrymen swear the marks keep their glow longer the deeper the gallery. On the lowest level, where the pumps gave out years ago, marks cut the spring before last are still burning.
items.name: Glow-Chalk (3 sticks)

dnd5e.mechanics: Marks most dry surfaces like ordinary chalk. For 1 hour after a mark is made, it sheds a pale green glow readable in darkness within 10 feet (it is not a light source and doesn't illuminate its surroundings). After the glow fades, the mark remains as an ordinary chalk mark — enduring about a month indoors, a day or two in weather. Each stick makes about 50 marks; three sticks per bundle.

pf2e.mechanics: Marks most dry surfaces like chalk. For 1 hour after marking, the mark glows faintly — legible in darkness from within 10 feet, though it sheds no usable light. Afterward it persists as an ordinary chalk mark, lasting about a month indoors or a day or two in weather. About 50 marks per stick; three sticks per bundle.

at_the_table: The light you can use while soaked, while hiding a heat source, or while standing in air that would turn a torch into a funeral.
Six hours of dim light is a whole watch: hang it over the camp and let the party argue about who sleeps under the glow.
items.description: A finger-length glass vial, cool to the touch even after hours in a pocket, with two liquids lying in lazy layers until shaken into a moon-pale glow. It gives off no heat, no smoke, and no smell — which is exactly what a miner wants three levels down where the air itself can catch. Spent vials are pierced and worn as pendants in pit towns, one per season survived.
items.hooks: A deep-shaft foreman has started buying spent vials back at double what a full one costs. He wants them unopened, unwashed, and he checks each one against his tongue.
items.name: Glowvial

dnd5e.mechanics: As a bonus action, shake to mix the reagents. The vial sheds dim light in a 10-ft radius for 6 hours. The light is cold and cannot ignite anything; it works underwater and in windy or gas-filled air where open flame would be dangerous or fatal.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 Interact action to shake and activate. Sheds dim light in a 10-ft radius for 6 hours. The glow produces no heat and no flame, functioning underwater and in flammable air where a torch cannot be safely lit.

at_the_table: Camp stops being downtime when someone has to boil water, change dressings, and sit with the wounded. The kit hands the quiet character a role.
Five poultices, six wounded. Somebody makes the call.
items.description: A waxed linen roll holding five cloth squares packed with comfrey, plantain leaf, and honey-soaked moss, warm-smelling even cold. Bound over a wound, the poultice draws heat through the night and comes away brown and stiff by morning. Most kits are sewn by the same hands that will one day lay their buyers out, and the stitching is done with the same care.
items.hooks: Every kit the midwife sells includes a sixth square, folded separately, unlabeled, and smelling of nothing at all. She says it's for the wound you don't show anyone.
items.name: Herbal Poultice Kit (five poultices)

dnd5e.mechanics: Over 10 minutes, bind one poultice over a patient's wounds; it works while they rest. If the patient spends Hit Dice during a rest taken with the poultice on, they treat any Hit Die roll of 1 or 2 as a 3. One poultice per patient per rest; no effect on a patient who doesn't rest.

pf2e.mechanics: 10 minutes to apply before a full night's rest. The patient treats their Constitution modifier as 1 higher (minimum +1) when calculating Hit Points regained from that night's rest. One poultice per patient per night; it provides no benefit without a full rest.

at_the_table: The reliable peace offering: handed to a crying child, a suspicious guard's kid, or a companion sulking at the far edge of the firelight.
A grizzled character caught keeping a private stash has been characterized in one sentence.
items.description: It has the heft and the give of a roof slate, and it takes a patient jaw or a hot cup to make any progress at all. Worked at long enough, it goes sweet at the edge and dense and nutty underneath, clover honey over woodsmoke. Bakers press each round with a flower stamp, and every town's stamp is different; travelers collect the patterns the way sailors collect ports. Children gnaw them for hours, and dwarves who claim to want nothing accept them without comment.
items.hooks: Every stamp in the region is registered with the bakers' guild except one — a seven-petaled flower that keeps turning up in bundles nobody remembers buying. The biscuits are excellent. The honey is from no hive anyone can name.
items.name: Honeyed Hardtack (bundle of six)

dnd5e.mechanics: One biscuit counts as part of a day's food. A creature that eats one during a short rest and regains hit points from spending Hit Dice regains 1 additional hit point — comfort, not medicine.

pf2e.mechanics: One biscuit counts as part of a day's rations. A creature that eats one while being Treated for Wounds recovers 1 additional Hit Point from that treatment — comfort, not medicine.

at_the_table: The classic beat, earned honestly: the estate's hounds come baying around the corner, and one player is already reaching for the pouch.
Eating your own escape plan on day four of a lean crossing is a decision players remember making.
items.description: The pouch opens with a punch of smoke, black pepper, and rendered fat that carries across a room — and farther than that on a night wind. Each strip chews slow and salty with a heat that builds at the back of the throat, cut from whatever the smokehouse hung that season. Hunters spice it hard on purpose: a scent that loud reads as food, not intruder, to every nose downwind.
items.hooks: The smokehouse keeper pays double for game brought in from the western ridge and asks each hunter the same question: did anything follow you down? He smokes that meat in a separate shed, sells it to no one, and burns the drippings.
items.name: Hunter's Spiced Jerky

dnd5e.mechanics: A pouch feeds one creature for two days, or serves another purpose: a strip tossed as a distraction gives a hound, wolf, or similar keen-nosed beast something better to think about, granting advantage on the next Dexterity (Stealth) check made to slip past it while it investigates.

pf2e.mechanics: A pouch feeds one creature for two days. A strip tossed as a distraction occupies a hound, wolf, or similar scent-keen animal for a few moments, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to the next Stealth check to Sneak past it while it investigates.

at_the_table: "We leave when the candle dies" turns an hour of dungeon time into a physical object on the table — and the blue minute is the tensest sixty seconds in the game.
Lighting one over a bargain, a confession, or a goodbye gives any scene a deadline the players can watch burn.
items.description: A slim candle of graded wax, ringed with a single black line at the shoulder and smelling faintly of myrrh. Chandlers burn one candle from every batch against a sandglass and stamp the base of its siblings only if it dies on the hour — a common candle costs a copper, but a candle you can swear by costs more. Watch-houses, vigils, and card games all keep time by the same small blue farewell.
items.hooks: The gaol's night-warden times confessions by last-candle: you have until it dies to talk, and his candles are known to run merciful and long. He buys them from a chandler whose shop no one has ever found open.
items.name: Last-Candles (pair)

dnd5e.mechanics: When lit in a sheltered space, a last-candle burns for exactly 1 hour, then gutters out; the flame sinks and turns blue for the final minute as a warning. While burning, it sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet, as a candle. Two per pair.

pf2e.mechanics: Once lit in a sheltered space, the candle burns for exactly 1 hour and extinguishes itself, the flame sinking and turning blue for its final minute. While it burns, it gives light as a candle (dim light in a 10-foot radius). Two per pair.

at_the_table: The party's line of red knots is a map they wrote themselves — and anything following them can read it too.
Finding a single ribbon of an unfamiliar color, deep in country the party believed unmapped, changes the expedition's whole posture.
Untying your ribbons on the way out is an hour of work and a real decision: leave the road open, or close it behind you.
items.description: Twenty strips of coarse linen boiled in dye and wax, stiff enough to crackle when you knot one to a branch. The color is a screaming madder-red that no leaf, lichen, or berry in any honest forest can match. Outfitters cut them from bolts woven for exactly this trade — where chalk washes off in the first rain, a ribbon hangs on and fades slow.
items.hooks: Three seasons of ribbon lines converge on the same ravine — three colors, three expeditions, none of whom ever met. None of them came back to collect their knots.
items.name: Marked Trail Ribbons (score of 20)

dnd5e.mechanics: Tie a ribbon as part of your movement. Ribbons stay visible and in place through rain, snow, and wind for about a month. A route you ribboned can be retraced without a check in ordinary conditions; in fog, darkness, or heavy snowfall, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to backtrack along it. Twenty ribbons per score.

pf2e.mechanics: Tie a ribbon with an Interact action. Ribbons endure weather for about a month. You automatically Sense Direction along a route you ribboned in ordinary conditions; in fog, darkness, or heavy snowfall, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to retrace it. Twenty ribbons per score.

at_the_table: Fifty words, waterproof, tied where only your ally will look: the party can now run schemes across distance and weather, and so can everyone else.
A found ribbon is evidence with a texture — who ties a message into a dead man's bootlace?
items.description: Five pale strips of tight-woven silk, boiled in oil and size until they take charcoal like slate and shed water like a duck. Unrolled, one crackles softly and smells of lamp oil and old rain. Couriers on the long routes trust them over paper the way sailors trust tar over paint — every ribbon carries a scrivener's counter-stamp at one end, so a forged drop is a hanging matter somewhere.
items.hooks: The drop-tree above the ford holds nine ribbons, all addressed to the same name, none collected. The newest knot is fresh this morning — and the ford has been washed out for a month.
items.name: Message Ribbons (bundle of 5)

dnd5e.mechanics: Write on a ribbon with charcoal, graphite, or ink; roll and tie it closed. The writing survives rain, immersion, mud, and freezing for about a month — a ribbon left at a drop, tied to a branch, or sewn into a hem arrives legible. Each ribbon holds about 50 words. Five per bundle.

pf2e.mechanics: Write on a ribbon with charcoal, graphite, or ink; roll and tie it closed. The writing remains legible through rain, immersion, and freezing for about a month. Each ribbon holds about 50 words. Five per bundle.

at_the_table: The arrow has to come out on the kitchen table, tonight. This jar decides whether that scene is screaming or conversation.
A numbed hand can grip a brand, a blade, or a rope of burning pitch without flinching — and won't notice the damage it's taking.
items.description: A gray-green paste of clove oil, mandrake leaf, and beeswax that tingles cold on your fingertips even through the wooden spatula. Where it touches, sensation folds up and leaves. Barber-surgeons scrape the jar with a marked stick — every workshop's stick shows the same worn groove at the two-dose line, the amount one soldier needs.
items.hooks: An interrogator in the low quarter buys the salve in bulk, and not for kindness: her subjects feel nothing while she works, and she describes each cut aloud. The ones she releases never speak of it above a whisper.
items.name: Numbing Salve (jar, four applications)

dnd5e.mechanics: Rub into an area of skin over 1 minute; it stays numb for 1 hour. A numbed patient automatically holds still through stitching, cautery, or the removal of an arrow or splinter, and Wisdom (Medicine) checks made on the numbed area have advantage. A numbed hand imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and delicate tool work.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 minute to apply; the area is numb for 1 hour. The patient doesn't need to attempt checks to remain still during surgery on the numbed area, and Medicine checks to treat that area gain a +1 circumstance bonus. A numbed hand takes a -2 circumstance penalty to Thievery checks and fine Interact tasks.

at_the_table: The universal stage business for a slow scene: two characters, one pipe, and the questions that only come out sideways.
Offering the first draw to a stranger is a truce older than most treaties; refusing it politely is a skill of its own.
items.description: The leaf is cut coarse and packs down under the thumb with a give that tells an old smoker whether it's been kept damp enough; too dry and it burns hot and fast, too wet and it sulks. The ritual matters more than the leaf — the packing, the passing, the silence between draws. Growers mark their harvest with a colored thread through the pouch string, and arguments over which valley's thread is best have outlived the arguers.
items.hooks: An old campaigner in the market square trades a bowl of his private blend for stories — one bowl, one story, no coin accepted. He never smokes his own bowl until the teller is out of sight, and he writes nothing down, and he has been asking for stories about one particular road.
items.name: Pipeweed Pouch

dnd5e.mechanics: A pouch holds about twenty bowls. Sharing a pipe takes ten unhurried minutes and is its own excuse to be somewhere: while two or more creatures share one, onlookers read them as idle rather than waiting, watching, or listening, and no check is needed to justify their presence. The smoke stays in wool and hair for a day, and anyone who knows the blend can place where you've been.

pf2e.mechanics: A pouch holds about twenty bowls. Sharing a pipe takes ten unhurried minutes and serves as its own pretext: while sharing, you and your companions need attempt no checks to explain loitering or waiting in a public place. The smoke clings to clothing and hair for a day, and a creature familiar with the blend can identify where it was grown.

at_the_table: Third day of rain, everyone soaked, exhaustion looming: the character who packed a fire-log is briefly the most important person in the wilderness.
A guaranteed fire is also a guaranteed signal — one brick can announce the party to everything downwind of its resin smoke.
items.description: A dense brick of sawdust, tallow, and pine resin, pressed hard enough to ring when you rap it and greasy enough to leave a shine on your palm. It smells of turpentine and candle stubs — chandlers press them from the sweepings of everything else they make. The scorched thumbprint stamped into one end is the presser's guarantee that it will light.
items.hooks: The best-pressed logs come out of one chandlery, and since midwinter they have burned with a thread of incense running through the smoke — the resin blend used at funerals and at nothing else. Her recipe hasn't changed. Her sweepings come from the same three shops they always have.
items.name: Pressed Fire-Log

dnd5e.mechanics: When lit with flint and steel or any open flame, the log catches in 1 round even in rain, wind, or with wet kindling — no check required. It burns for 1 hour, hot enough to dry and ignite damp firewood stacked over it, and sustains a normal campfire's light and warmth.

pf2e.mechanics: Light it with a firestarter or open flame as a 1-minute activity; it ignites automatically even in rain or wind, with no flat check. It burns 1 hour, hot enough to catch damp firewood laid over it, providing a campfire's light and warmth.

at_the_table: The poisoned banquet is a race: who realizes in time, who has a vial, and who's too proud to use it in front of the duke's guests.
The smuggler who swallowed the evidence knows the party knows. Producing the vial ends the standoff without a blade drawn.
items.description: A squat clay vial of mustard water, powdered ipecac root, and brine, smelling exactly like what it's about to make you do. It works fast, loud, and without dignity. Taster's guilds issue one to every member on the first day, along with the advice stitched inside the kit: better emptied than buried.
items.hooks: A pickpocket in the fish market swallowed a signet ring two days ago and has since drunk four purgatives. All four came up empty, and she can feel the ring moving — upward.
items.name: Purgative Draught

dnd5e.mechanics: Drink as an action; within 1 minute you vomit violently. Make a new saving throw against one ingested poison or contaminant affecting you, with advantage, and any swallowed object smaller than a fist comes up with the rest. You are poisoned until the end of your next turn and can't benefit from another purgative for 24 hours.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 Interact action to drink; you retch within 1 minute. Attempt a new Fortitude save with a +2 circumstance bonus against one ingested poison affecting you, and any swallowed object smaller than a fist is expelled. You are sickened 1 (can't reduce it for 10 minutes) and can't benefit from another purgative for 24 hours.

at_the_table: The sea-fort's every hinge is scaled orange; the party with a tin doesn't force doors, it schedules them — one fizzing minute apiece, quietly.
A sword rusted into its scabbard, freed on the spot, hands a family heirloom back its dignity — and its edge.
items.description: A shallow tin of gray-brown paste that stings the nose like vinegar poured over a forge. Worked into a seized hinge it fizzes, weeps orange, and leaves the metal bare, bright, and hungry-looking — smiths warn you to oil whatever it touches within the day. The underside of most tins carries a previous owner's scratch-tally of doors that owed it their opening.
items.hooks: The smith refuses to sell the paste to anyone bound for the drowned fort, and won't discuss it. The last tin that went out there came back with a peddler — scraped empty, and the owner's name filed off the lid.
items.name: Rust-Eater Paste (tin of 5 uses)

dnd5e.mechanics: Apply 1 use to a rusted or corrosion-seized metal object — a hinge, lock, buckle, valve, or blade fused in its scabbard — and wait 1 minute. The mechanism then moves freely without a check, or, if it is also stuck for another reason (warped, barred, wedged), grants advantage on the Strength check to force it. It doesn't repair structural damage or affect magical corrosion. Five uses per tin.

pf2e.mechanics: Apply 1 use to a rusted or corrosion-seized metal mechanism with an Interact action and wait 1 minute. The mechanism then operates freely without a check; if it's also stuck for a non-rust reason, the paste instead grants a +2 circumstance bonus to the Athletics check to Force Open it. It doesn't repair damage or counteract magical corrosion. Five uses per tin.

at_the_table: The baying behind the party goes confused, then circular, then silent — a chase scene ended by one pouch and a river the dogs never needed.
Dusting the whole party before a warren crawl costs a handful of coin and buys an hour of walking past things with better noses than eyes.
items.description: A doeskin pouch of powder the color of dried mustard, odorless to you, which is the unsettling part — your nose keeps reaching for it and finding nothing. It dusts on fine as pollen and deadens every smell you carry: sweat, woodsmoke, fear. Old huntsmen sew a pinch into their collars before wolf country, a habit their grandmothers called paying the toll.
items.hooks: Somewhere upriver is a hollow where nothing has a smell — not the moss, not the water, not the deer carcass that should have drawn flies a week ago.
items.name: Scent-Killer

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, crush the pouch and dust yourself or one willing creature. For 1 hour, creatures that rely on smell have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks to detect or track the dusted creature by scent, and cannot track it by scent alone.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 Interact action to dust yourself or an adjacent willing creature. For 1 hour, the dusted creature is hidden from imprecise scent, and creatures using scent to Track it take a -2 circumstance penalty to their Survival checks.

at_the_table: The wizard is face-down, the ritual is at the third verse, and one round is the whole negotiation. Pop the cork.
Passing the vial under a "sleeping" sentry's nose settles the question of whether the drink was drugged — publicly, and in one breath.
items.description: A stubby glass vial of ammoniac crystals and crushed hartshorn under a cork you learn to loosen one-handed. Unstoppered, it hits like a slap made of smell — eyes water at arm's length. Duelists' seconds carry one on a neck cord, and an old vial's cork bears a tooth-mark for every morning it was needed.
items.hooks: A collier's boy pulled from the flooded shaft coughed, breathed, and slept — and has slept for nine days since. His mother has bought salts from every shop in town, and last market-day she started buying them in other towns.
items.name: Smelling Salts (vial, ten uses)

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, wave the vial under the nose of an adjacent creature. A creature unconscious from sleep, drink, or a nonmagical knockout wakes immediately, and a creature making death saving throws has advantage on its next one. The salts don't restore hit points and can't rouse a creature unconscious from being at 0 hit points.

pf2e.mechanics: 1 Interact action. An adjacent creature that is unconscious but not dying wakes immediately. A dying creature gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its next recovery check. The salts restore no Hit Points and don't end the dying condition.

at_the_table: The exit line: one round of chaos is exactly enough time to drop through the trapdoor, and everyone at the table knows it.
Thrown at an archer's feet instead of your own, it turns a killing lane into a guessing game.
items.description: A wax-paper ball no bigger than a plum, packed so tight it creaks between your fingers, smelling faintly of pitch and burnt sugar. Crush it and the smoke arrives all at once, gray-white and greasy, clinging to wool for days. Stage companies buy them in bulk, which is why half the pellets in circulation are dyed a theatrical crimson.
items.hooks: The good ones come from a widow who sells at night, in singles, and only after she has watched you cross the square twice. She dyes her own the theater crimson and has never sold to anyone in daylight. Every so often a crimson pellet goes off somewhere in the city at noon, and she shutters her windows for the rest of the week.
items.name: Smoke Pellet

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, crush and drop at your feet or throw up to 20 ft. Thick smoke fills a 10-ft-radius sphere, heavily obscuring the area until the start of your next turn, then lightly obscuring it for 1 more round before dispersing. A moderate wind clears it immediately.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (thrown Interact, 20 ft.). Smoke fills a 10-ft burst; creatures in it are concealed until the start of your next turn, then the smoke thins and disperses at the end of that round. Strong wind ends the effect.

at_the_table: Rations run out three days before the map does; the snare coil turns that from a crisis into a routine, and the party's camp into a place with work to do at dusk.
Checking the snare line at dawn is a scene generator: sometimes breakfast, sometimes tracks, sometimes something has checked the line first.
items.description: A palm-sized coil of drawn brass wire, bright where your fingers have worked it and dull where it has waited in the pouch. It kinks if you rush it and sings a thin note when a loop pulls true. Village trappers braid a hair from their first catch into the binding cord — wire that has fed someone once, they say, remembers how.
items.hooks: The trapper sells the coil cheap and asks one thing in return: set nothing north of the split oak. His own snares up there come back sprung, licked clean, and neatly re-set.
items.name: Snare Wire Coil (20 snares)

dnd5e.mechanics: Spend 1 hour during a rest setting snares along game trails, then make a Wisdom (Survival) check: DC 10 in ordinary country, DC 15 in barren or picked-over land. On a success, the snares yield enough small game by morning to feed one creature for a day, plus one more creature for every 5 points the check exceeds the DC. Each setting expends wire for 2 snares; the coil holds 20.

pf2e.mechanics: Spend 1 hour setting snares during rest, then attempt a Survival check to Subsist: DC 15 in ordinary country, DC 20 in barren land. On a success, the snares provide subsistence living for one creature by morning (two on a critical success) without further foraging. Each setting expends wire for 2 snares; the coil holds 20.

at_the_table: Passed down a line of frightened militia before the gates open — courage by the mouthful, with the morning already mortgaged.
The negotiation lubricant that works on both sides of the table, and the character who refuses a poured measure has made a statement everyone noticed.
One measure is a choice; the second is a scene.
items.description: The flask is pewter and sweats cold in the hand, its four measures scored inside the neck so you can feel what's left without looking. It tastes of dark fruit for one heartbeat and of fire for the next ten, settling into a warmth that spreads from the sternum outward. Vintners in the high valleys fortify their pressings for winters that kill unfortified wine in the barrel, and they seal each flask with a thumbprint in the wax.
items.hooks: Who keeps buying the vintner's entire winter stock before it reaches market? The carter who hauls it away takes the same road every month — the one that ends at a shrine where no one lives, where the empty flasks come back washed.
items.name: Strongwine Flask

dnd5e.mechanics: A flask holds four measures. For 1 hour after drinking a measure, a creature has advantage on saving throws against being frightened and disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. A second measure within that hour extends both to 4 hours and adds disadvantage on Dexterity checks. A third leaves the creature poisoned until it finishes a long rest.

pf2e.mechanics: A flask holds four measures. For 1 hour after drinking a measure, a creature gains a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against fear and takes a -1 circumstance penalty to Perception. A second measure within that hour extends both to 4 hours and adds a -1 circumstance penalty to Reflex saves. A third leaves the drinker sickened 2 until their next daily preparations.

at_the_table: The cheapest miracle in the pack: produced at the right moment, it stops a child's tears, a mob's youngest thrower, or a fey court's laughter — briefly.
Twelve figures, twelve bought moments — and a clever player spends them one at a time, knowing exactly how long a sweet lasts.
items.description: Each figure weighs nothing in the palm and chimes faintly against its neighbors when the box is tilted — spun sugar, thin as eggshell, tinted with berry juice and poured into molds carved by confectioners who guard the patterns like heirlooms. On the tongue each dissolves into a sweetness with one hidden note: anise in the dancer, ginger in the knight, something like rain in the swan. Held to the light, a good figure glows.
items.hooks: What does the confectioner's newest mold depict? Buyers describe it differently — a tower, a gate, a figure waving — but every child who eats one has the same dream that night, and lately a few of them wave back.
items.name: Sugar Figures (box of twelve)

dnd5e.mechanics: Offering a figure to a child, or to a fey creature of a whimsical bent, buys a moment rather than a bonus: for as long as the figure lasts on the tongue, the recipient listens, and raises no hand, no alarm, and no price. Its attitude is unchanged once the sugar is gone.

pf2e.mechanics: Offering a figure to a child or a whimsically inclined fey buys a moment rather than a bonus: while the figure dissolves, the recipient listens, takes no hostile action, raises no alarm, and names no price. Its attitude is unchanged when the sugar is gone.

at_the_table: Poured across the doorway behind a fleeing party, it converts one round of running into a whole scene of swearing.
Laid before a fight, it turns the obvious charge lane into a trap the players designed themselves.
items.description: A dried gourd of amber sap that smells of pine and spoiled honey, heavy and slow when you tilt it, like a thought it hasn't finished. It pours in one reluctant sheet and grips anything that presses into it — boot, hoof, or hand. Poachers score the gourds with a thumbnail cross so they can tell theirs from a rival's at a glance.
items.hooks: Every gourd sold this season grips harder than last year's stock. Walk out to the grove she taps and the ground beneath each tree is swept bare and packed smooth, in a circle exactly as wide as the branches reach, with nothing fallen anywhere inside it.
items.name: Tanglefoot Sap

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, pour or hurl the gourd up to 20 ft. The sap coats one 5-ft square and stays sticky for 10 minutes. That square is difficult terrain, and a creature entering it must succeed on a DC 10 Strength saving throw or have its speed halved until the end of its next turn while it tears free.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (thrown Interact, 20 ft.). Coats one 5-ft square with adhesive sap for 10 minutes. The square is difficult terrain; a creature entering it must succeed at a DC 15 Reflex save or take a -10-ft status penalty to its Speed until the end of its next turn.

at_the_table: The gate guard's price isn't posted, but everyone on the river knows it: two thumb-widths, cut with your own knife, offered before you ask anything.
Sharing a pipe afterward slows a scene down on purpose — information arrives at the speed of smoke.
items.description: A rope of cured leaf as long as your forearm, twisted tight, sticky with molasses and smelling of sweet smoke and cellar dark. Out past the last mile-marker it spends better than silver — coin needs a market, but a pipe needs only an evening. Sutlers score each twist into thumb-widths, because that is the denomination in which favors are made.
items.hooks: The ferry guards, the toll-keeper, and the hermit at the pass all take twist tobacco — and all of them, without conferring, refuse the batch tied with blue thread. None of them can say who warned them off it.
items.name: Trade Tobacco Twist

dnd5e.mechanics: A twist is scored into about twelve thumb-widths, and past the last mile-marker that is the coin of the country: one thumb-width is the going rate for a night's shelter, a ferry crossing, an hour of a guide's time, or one question answered. Cut and offered before you ask, it settles the price with no haggling and no check. Offered afterward, it's a bribe, and everyone present will understand it as one.

pf2e.mechanics: A twist is scored into about twelve thumb-widths, the working currency past the last trading post: one thumb-width covers a night's shelter, a ferry crossing, an hour of a guide's time, or one answered question. Offered before you ask, it sets the price without a check and ends the haggling. Offered afterward, it's a bribe and is understood as one.

at_the_table: Twenty days into a wilderness arc, the character who produces this tin becomes the most popular person in camp.
The grim version: the stores turned four days ago, everyone knows it, and the tin is the only reason anyone is still eating. Seasoning bad meat is a decision, and the table will feel it.
When the tin runs empty, so does something in the party's mood — a soft clock the DM can hear ticking.
items.description: The tin sits in the palm heavier than its size promises, its lid held by a bayonet catch that opens with two fingers and a quarter turn — a fitting cut for cold hands. A pinch turns twice-baked biscuit and salt meat into something you'd eat by choice, not necessity. Scratched across the inside of the lid is a previous owner's blend, written out in a hand that got smaller as it ran out of room.
items.hooks: Caravan cooks talk about the ninth pinch: pepper, clove, and one thing nobody has ever placed. It isn't sold. It turns up in tins bought secondhand, always a single pinch of it lying on top of the rest, and no two people who've found one agree on whether it was there when they bought the tin.
items.name: Traveler's Spice Tin

dnd5e.mechanics: A full tin seasons about twenty meals. A pinch masks the taste of stores that have turned: a creature will willingly eat a seasoned ration that has gone bad, and has advantage on the saving throw against its spoilage. The spice makes bad food edible, not safe.

pf2e.mechanics: A full tin seasons about twenty meals. A pinch masks the taste of spoiled stores: a creature will willingly eat seasoned rations that have turned, and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the Fortitude save against their effects. The spice hides the spoilage; it doesn't undo it.

at_the_table: The cellar's carpet of rats parts like a curtain, which is when everyone sees what the rats were covering.
Lighting one before camping in a ruin is the veteran move that tells new players who at this table has been bitten before.
items.description: A gray cone the size of a spinning top, smelling of bitter herbs and something sharper underneath that makes your eyes prickle before it's even lit. It burns from the tip down in a slow ashen spiral, and everything small and many-legged decides at once to be elsewhere. Granary wardens stamp the base of theirs with the harvest year — a cellar cleared with old stock is a cellar not cleared at all.
items.hooks: The last granary warden to burn a cone in the undercroft came up the stairs at a run and paid a mason, that same afternoon, to brick the doorway shut.
items.name: Vermin Smoke

dnd5e.mechanics: As an action, light the cone and set it down. Acrid smoke fills a 20-ft-radius area over 1 minute and lingers for 10 minutes. Ordinary rats, insects, spiders, and similar pests flee the area; a swarm of such creatures must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw at the start of each of its turns in the smoke or use its movement to leave by the shortest route. Harmless to larger creatures beyond stinging eyes.

pf2e.mechanics: Held alchemical item, 1 action to Activate (Interact, light and place). Smoke spreads to fill a 20-ft emanation over 1 minute and lingers for 10 minutes. Ordinary vermin flee; a swarm in the smoke must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save at the start of each of its turns or spend its movement leaving the area. Larger creatures suffer no effect beyond watering eyes.

at_the_table: The all-night vigil, the third watch, the ambush the party refuses to sleep through: wakeleaf makes staying awake a choice with a bill attached.
A gray-gummed stranger who never seems to sleep raises a fair question: what are they afraid of missing?
items.description: Narrow silver-green leaves that crackle like paper and taste of pepper and green walnut husk. Your heart notices before your head does. Career sentries chew it until their gums stain gray at the line — a mark garrison sergeants check for at muster, the way they check boots.
items.hooks: Why does the night warden at the granary go through a pouch a night, every night, when nothing has been stolen in years? Her requisition slips stopped saying what she's watching for.
items.name: Wakeleaf (pouch of five)

dnd5e.mechanics: Chew one leaf as an action. For 4 hours, you can't fall asleep and have advantage on saving throws against magical sleep. If you use wakeleaf on two or more consecutive nights, you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Insight) checks until you finish a long rest without it.

pf2e.mechanics: Interact to chew. For 4 hours, you can't fall asleep naturally and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against sleep effects. Using wakeleaf on consecutive nights makes you fatigued when it wears off, and the fatigue can't be removed until you sleep a full night without it.

at_the_table: The swamp stops being a wall and becomes a road: the party can drink where pursuers can't follow.
Ten doses, six people, a two-week crossing — the arithmetic on the vial is a quiet countdown the whole table can feel.
items.description: A finger-length glass vial of amber liquid that reeks of vinegar and crushed juniper the moment you thumb the stopper. One dose turns a gallon of green marsh water briefly cloudy, then clear, with a gray sediment settling like ash. Mission-posts hand vials out along fever rivers, each one etched with a tally of the outbreaks it has outlived.
items.hooks: A downriver village has begun ordering the drops by the crate — every household, every week, more than any well could foul and more than all of them together could drink. They aren't drinking it. They carry it upstream at dusk, all of them at once, and pour it into the river.
items.name: Water Purification Drops (vial of 10 doses)

dnd5e.mechanics: Add 1 dose to up to 1 gallon of water and wait 10 minutes: foul, stagnant, or contaminated water becomes safe to drink, and drinking it can't inflict disease. The drops have no effect on poison added deliberately or on magical contamination. Ten doses per vial.

pf2e.mechanics: Add 1 dose to up to 1 gallon of water and wait 10 minutes: the water becomes potable, and drinking it can't expose you to disease. The drops don't counteract deliberate poisoning or magical contamination. Ten doses per vial.

at_the_table: The river crossing goes wrong for everyone except the character whose spellbook comes out of the water dry.
One tin before the wet season is cheap; remembering it during the wet season is character development.
items.description: A shallow tin of translucent amber paste that smells of pine tar and beeswax and warms to spreadable under a thumb. Brushed into leather or seam-stitching it sinks in and vanishes, leaving only a faint shine and the sound of rain giving up. Coastal cobblers score the tin's lid with the month of sale — a courtesy, and a quiet reminder to come back before the autumn storms.
items.hooks: A drowned courier washed ashore with everything ruined except the scroll case at her belt, sealed with a resin no chandler on the coast can identify. The letter inside is addressed to a woman by name — and every record in the port agrees that she drowned forty years ago.
items.name: Waterproofing Resin

dnd5e.mechanics: Applied over 10 minutes to one pair of boots, one garment's seams, or one container up to scroll-case size, then cured overnight. For roughly three months, the treated item and its contents stay dry through rain, fording, and brief submersion. Prolonged submersion (more than 1 hour) or fire damage ends the seal.

pf2e.mechanics: Apply over 10 minutes (Interact) to one pair of boots, one garment's seams, or one container of scroll-case size or smaller; cures overnight. For about three months, the item and its contents remain dry through rain, fording, and brief submersion. Submersion longer than 1 hour or any fire damage ends the treatment.

at_the_table: On day four of the march, the character passing strips down the line is the one holding the party together.
A bitten-down wad in a corpse's cheek says this person walked a long way in pain — and kept going.
items.description: Finger-length strips of pale inner bark, bitter enough to pucker your whole jaw before the dull warmth spreads. Every pouch smells of riverbanks and rain. Old soldiers can tell upland bark from lowland by the aftertaste, and they argue about it the way other people argue about wine.
items.hooks: Old soldiers argue upland bark against lowland by the aftertaste, and agree on one point: take nothing off the willows below the old ford. Those trees are the largest in the country, and their bark strips away sweet instead of bitter — and one strip of it dulls a pain you had not noticed you were carrying.
items.name: Willowbark Chew (pouch of ten)

dnd5e.mechanics: Chew one strip for 1 minute. For the next 4 hours, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws against gaining exhaustion from forced marches, and pain from an existing nonmagical injury imposes no disadvantage on ability checks. Doesn't restore hit points or remove exhaustion already gained.

pf2e.mechanics: Interact to chew for 1 minute. For 4 hours, gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves against fatigue from overland travel, and you ignore circumstance penalties to skill checks caused by pain from untreated nonmagical wounds.

at_the_table: The nightly hang is a ritual that builds the wilderness: ten minutes of throwing, cursing, and hauling, and the forest feels real. The night the party skips it is the night the DM has been waiting for.
Claw marks eight feet up the hanging tree, higher than yesterday's, turn a routine camp chore into the session's quietest dread.
items.description: The sack smells of tar and old bacon fat no matter how new it is, and the cord is waxed stiff so wet bark won't bind it. A tin tag on the drawstring is stamped with a crude bear, teeth bared — the outfitter's joke, or warning. The throwing weight is a river stone in a leather net, worn glossy by a hundred cold-fingered tosses over a hundred branches.
items.hooks: In one valley the hangs have stopped working. Bags strung well above any bear's reach are found emptied — lowered, unpacked, and hauled back up, with the knots retied. Retied better.
items.name: Bear-Bag Kit

dnd5e.mechanics: A 50-ft. waxed cord, throwing weight, and tarred canvas sack holding a week's provisions for four. Hanging the bag takes 10 minutes and a DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) check. On a success, the food hangs beyond the reach of climbing and jumping beasts, and scent-drawn predators investigate the bag rather than the sleepers; on a failure, the party finds out which at dawn.

pf2e.mechanics: Waxed 50-foot cord, throwing weight, and tarred sack holding a week's provisions for four. Hanging it takes 10 minutes and a DC 15 Survival check. Success keeps provisions out of reach of animals and draws scent-hunting predators to the bag instead of the camp; on a failure, the hang looks right but isn't.

at_the_table: Coin discipline as play: the walking-around pouch, the real pouch, and the one nobody mentions. A cutpurse gets the first and thinks the job is done.
Gate guards who find the hidden pouch don't care that it's empty. They care that you own it.
items.description: Three pouches off the same hide, the leather still smelling of the tannery, with drawstrings waxed so they hold a knot. Two are honest working pouches, sized for coin and flint. The third is cut flat and pale, made to lie against the skin and be forgotten — by everyone.
items.hooks: The flat pouch rides against the skin, which is why the weir-keeper's men search for one before they search for a purse. The body they pulled last week had the flat pouch and nothing else — no coin, no belt, no working pouches at all. The one nobody was meant to find had been moved around to the outside.
items.name: Belt Pouch Set (three)

dnd5e.mechanics: Three matched belt pouches, each holding 6 lb. or one-fifth of a cubic foot. The third is cut flat to ride unseen inside a waistband; finding it on a search of your person requires a DC 12 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check.

pf2e.mechanics: Three belt pouches. The third is a flat concealed pouch: a creature Searching you must succeed at a DC 15 Perception check to find it.

at_the_table: The cheapest way a split party stays a party. Agreeing on the signal code is a five-minute scene that pays off for a whole campaign.
One long blast in the dark, from a direction where no ally should be, is a full encounter hook by itself.
items.description: Carved from a deer's leg bone and polished smooth by years of pockets, with a tone that carries flat and hard through fog and tree cover. Every region's hunters cut the mouthpiece a little differently — a keen ear can tell where a whistle was made by its pitch.
items.hooks: Poachers in the nearby forest have started answering the local hunters' whistle codes — correctly. Someone taught them, and the hunting lodge wants to know who traded away their voice.
items.name: Bone Signal Whistle

dnd5e.mechanics: Audible up to 600 feet outdoors in calm conditions. A set of agreed signals lets allies communicate simple one-word concepts (danger, come, hold, flee) without shared line of sight.

pf2e.mechanics: Audible up to 600 feet outdoors. Pre-arranged signals can convey a single simple concept per blast pattern.

at_the_table: The deed, the treaty, or the spell scroll survives the burning building. The building is negotiable; the paper isn't.
Six turns to open means no one reads the contents in a hurry, in the rain, with the guards coming — which is exactly why nervous couriers love it.
items.description: A heavy brass cylinder with a threaded cap, polished to a shine by pocket and saddlebag alike. It takes six full turns to open — a small, deliberate ritual — and closes with a click you can feel in your teeth. The metal always carries the temperature of wherever it's been.
items.hooks: Scriveners' apprentices whisper that one workshop cuts its tube threads a half-turn shallow, so a rapped tube sounds subtly different when the cap has been opened and rethreaded by a stranger. The workshop denies making anything of the kind, which is what you'd want them to say.
items.name: Brass Scroll Tube

dnd5e.mechanics: Holds up to six rolled sheets of paper or parchment. Contents are unharmed by fire and heat, including a creature's breath weapon. After exposure to open flame the tube stays searing hot for 10 minutes; opening it barehanded before then deals 1 fire damage.

pf2e.mechanics: Holds six rolled sheets. Contents are immune to fire damage. After the tube is exposed to fire it remains hot for 10 minutes; handling it unprotected deals 1 fire damage.

at_the_table: The rearguard's best friend: a scattered bag turns "they're chasing us" into "they *were* chasing us." Retreats become plays, not routs.
Sown in the dark behind a camp or across a windowsill, caltrops are the alarm that also bites. Sweeping them back up afterward — one by one, by hand — is its own scene.
items.description: Twenty four-spiked iron stars in a drawstring bag, forged so one point always stands up however they land — the blacksmith's little proof that geometry holds grudges. These are quarry-forge work: fast, ugly, and sharp enough to find a boot sole through mud. The bag clinks like bad news being counted.
items.hooks: A caravan trader sells caltrops with the tips blackened, "for night work," and swears the tar is just tar. The last company that bought a bag reports every guard who stepped on one slept three days — and one of them still talks about the dream they all shared.
items.name: Caltrops (bag of 20)

dnd5e.mechanics: As the SRD item: an action spreads the bag over a 5-foot square. A creature entering the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or stop moving and take 1 piercing damage; until it regains at least 1 hit point, its walking speed is reduced by 10 feet.

pf2e.mechanics: As the caltrops item in the core rules: scatter into an adjacent 5-foot square; creatures moving through take piercing damage and a speed penalty on a failed save, per the standard item.

at_the_table: Whoever cooks holds power no class feature grants: the night the ranger makes the dead merchant's recipe is the night the party finally talks about him.
Hot food after a bad day is the DM's cheapest scene-setter — the smell of onions in fat says "you are safe for now" better than any narration.
items.description: Copper and tin nested like a puzzle, everything riding inside the big pot, the whole bundle chiming softly with each step of the mule. The pan is black with honest carbon and the ladle's handle has been wrapped in wire where somebody's grip wore through the wood. Unpacked, it turns any flat rock into a kitchen in the time it takes to argue about firewood.
items.hooks: The tinker's stock came off a wagon he bought whole at auction, kitchen and all. The pot's underside is engraved with eleven sets of initials, each struck through except the last — and the auction listed the wagon's owners as a family of four.
items.name: Camp Kitchen

dnd5e.mechanics: A nested bundle: pot, pan, kettle, ladle, knives, and mess tins for six. Counts as cook's utensils. A character proficient with cook's utensils who prepares a hot evening meal with it gives each diner advantage on their first saving throw against exhaustion before their next long rest.

pf2e.mechanics: Nested cookware serving up to six. Counts as the cooking gear needed to Subsist with Survival, and lets one check Subsist for up to six creatures where ingredients allow. A hot meal prepared during daily preparations grants each diner a +1 circumstance bonus to their next save against fatigue before their next daily preparations.

at_the_table: The contact won't talk to strangers, but he'll play anyone. Three games in, the party knows how he lies; he knows how they lose.
Downtime with stakes: copper wagers, table talk, and the one guard who keeps losing on purpose to stay in the conversation.
items.description: Boxwood and bog-oak pieces in a hinged board that smells of lamp smoke and spilled ale, the halves closing with a worn wooden click. Each piece is hand-cut, and the carver gave them faces — the mounted piece scowls, the tower has a door left open a crack. The paint on the pieces most often captured has been thumbed away to bare wood.
items.hooks: Look closer at the carved faces and you'll find they aren't invented — regulars at the gambling den can name half of them, laughing, pointing across the room. Nobody laughs at the sovereign piece. The man it's carved from hasn't been seen since the set went up for sale, and his piece is the one the carver cut a blindfold on.
items.name: Carved Game Set

dnd5e.mechanics: Counts as a gaming set. A match takes 10–30 minutes and is resolved as opposed gaming set checks, with stakes agreed beforehand. During a match, you can make one Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your opponent's Charisma (Deception) to read their temperament, honesty, or attention — win or lose the game.

pf2e.mechanics: A gaming set for social play and gambling; a match is resolved with opposed Games Lore or Society checks, with stakes set beforehand. During a match, you can Sense Motive against your opponent, and the relaxed setting means they don't grow suspicious on your failure (though on a critical failure you misread them as usual).

at_the_table: The classic maze-crawler's insurance: arrows at junctions, tallies on doors, a rendezvous mark only allies understand.
Finding someone else's chalk marks in a "sealed" tomb rewrites the whole expedition in one image.
items.description: Ten stubby sticks of pressed white chalk wrapped in twine, shedding pale dust into whatever pouch carries them. Quarry chalk is coarse and bright; scrivener's chalk is finer and squeaks. Either kind vanishes under a wet thumb — which is sometimes the entire point.
items.hooks: Down in the sewer junctions, someone has been correcting the smugglers' chalk codes — crossing out true routes and drawing new arrows toward the old cistern. The smugglers assume a rival gang. The chalk dust at each mark is mixed with grave soil.
items.name: Chalk Bundle (10 sticks)

dnd5e.mechanics: Marks most dry surfaces. Marks endure roughly a month indoors, a day or two exposed to weather. Ten sticks; each stick makes about 100 short marks.

pf2e.mechanics: Marks most dry surfaces; marks endure roughly a month indoors or a day or two in weather. Ten sticks per bundle.

at_the_table: The wizard in traveling silks realizes the whole market went quiet when the party walked in, and the ragpicker's stall is suddenly the most important shop in town.
Handing a bundle to the rescued prisoner: the moment they stop looking like what was done to them.
items.description: A shirt, trousers, a laced overtunic, and a cap, rolled in twine and smelling of the lye they were boiled in between owners. The cloth is patched at the elbows and knees in the way everyone here patches — which is the entire point of buying it. One cuff still carries a mend in someone else's thread, finer than the garment deserves.
items.hooks: Where does a ragpicker get clean, whole clothing in every size, restocked weekly? This one buys from the gravedigger's boy, and a bundle sold last market day matched — down to the mended cuff — the description a searching mother has been reading aloud at the fountain each morning.
items.name: Common Clothes Bundle

dnd5e.mechanics: As common clothes, cut and worn in the local style. While dressed from a bundle bought in the region, your outfit never gives away that you're an outsider — Charisma (Deception) checks to pass as an unremarkable local aren't made with disadvantage on account of your dress.

pf2e.mechanics: As ordinary clothing in the regional cut. While wearing a locally bought bundle, your clothes support an Impersonate attempt to pass as a generic local without needing a disguise kit for the outfit itself.

at_the_table: Ten minutes behind a locked door with the mirror, and the party's wanted man walks out gray-haired, stooped, and ignored.
The kit itself is evidence: any guard who finds one in your bags stops caring what your face looks like now.
items.description: A shallow wooden box that smells of greasepaint, spirit gum, and singed hair the moment the lid lifts. Inside: tiered trays of tinted paste, a mirror in the lid, dye bottles with wax-sealed stoppers, curls of human hair sorted by shade, and a lump of nose putty with somebody's old thumbprint still in it. The tray corners are worn round — this box has been opened in the dark, in a hurry, many times.
items.hooks: The theater costumer who assembled this kit recognizes her own work the way a smith knows his blades. The new wanted poster in the square shows a merchant who defrauded the grain exchange — and she recognizes the nose. She sold that face, and she remembers to whom.
items.name: Disguise Kit

dnd5e.mechanics: As a disguise kit: proficiency lets you add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made to create a visual disguise. The box holds cosmetics and greasepaint, hair dye, spirit gum, wig and beard stock, nose putty, and padding — supplies for roughly ten disguises before restocking (10 gp). Creating a disguise takes 10 minutes; a rushed 1-minute job gives disadvantage on the check.

pf2e.mechanics: As a disguise kit: required to Impersonate with a full visual disguise without penalty. Contains cosmetics, dyes, spirit gum, hair pieces, putty, and padding for roughly ten disguises; replacement cosmetics cost 1 gp per use. A disguise takes 10 minutes to apply.

at_the_table: The customs shed scene: the officer paws through spare shirts and a cheap lantern, and the party makes pleasant conversation over four inches of felony.
Bought secondhand, the first question is the best one — is the compartment empty?
items.description: An unremarkable traveling chest in scuffed pine, deliberately shabbier outside than in. The false floor sits on a bed of felt and lifts only when two brass studs are pressed together — a motion that looks like nothing at all. Tap it wherever you like; the carpenter packed the void's edges with sand so it thuds like solid wood.
items.hooks: An estate sale is offering the late magistrate's luggage, and one chest weighs three pounds more than its twin. The magistrate spent thirty years hearing smuggling cases. His widow set the price low, and she watches — closely — who buys that one.
items.name: False-Bottom Chest

dnd5e.mechanics: As a chest. The hidden compartment beneath the false floor holds 20 lb. in a 4-inch depth and requires a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check to find. A hurried search — customs at the gate, bandits on a schedule — doesn't get a check.

pf2e.mechanics: As a chest with a concealed compartment (1 Bulk capacity). Finding it requires a DC 20 Perception check while Searching the chest; creatures who merely open and rifle it don't get a check.

at_the_table: The night infiltration where the whole party crouches frozen — except the one whose pack didn't clink.
Reaching back and producing the rope, the potion, or the crowbar *right now*, while everyone else digs.
items.description: Oiled leather over a light ash frame, every buckle wrapped in felt and every strap ending in a leather keeper instead of a loose flap. Shake it fully loaded and you hear nothing but your own breathing. Inside, a dozen sewn loops and pockets hold each piece of gear exactly where your hand already knows it is.
items.hooks: The loop-and-pocket layout inside is a leatherworkers' guild pattern, identical in every pack they make — which is why a fence in the city pays double for them. Her burglars train on one pack and can rob the contents of any other blind.
items.name: Fine Backpack

dnd5e.mechanics: As a backpack. Stowed gear makes no sound when you move, and you can retrieve any one item from it with your free object interaction without stopping to search, even in darkness.

pf2e.mechanics: As a backpack. Contents don't rattle or clink (no penalty to Avoid Notice from stowed gear), and retrieving an item from it is a single Interact action rather than two.

at_the_table: The round where the alchemist's answer is already in hand while everyone else is rummaging.
Eight visible vials across the chest is a message read differently by guards, by tavern crowds, and by anything that's been burned before. Wearing it openly is a choice.
items.description: Supple harness leather with eight felt-throated loops, each holding a vial in a grip that releases to a practiced pull and to nothing else. The buckle sits off-center so nothing crosses your draw. Old stains around the third loop suggest the previous owner favored something that smoked.
items.hooks: An alchemist gives a free bandolier to every regular customer — generous, until you notice the loops are sized precisely to her vials and no one else's. Her competitors' bottles don't fit. Neither does the antidote sold across the street.
items.name: Fine Bandolier

dnd5e.mechanics: Worn across the chest; holds eight vials, flasks, or similarly small items. Drawing one is a free object interaction, and the padded loops keep stowed containers from shattering when you fall or are knocked prone.
